How wind chill is calculated

Estimate the US National Weather Service wind-chill temperature from air temperature in Fahrenheit and wind speed in miles per hour. The index applies only at or below 50°F with wind above 3 mph and assumes shade; sun exposure can change how conditions feel. At 30°F with 10 mph wind, the standard equation gives a wind chill near 21°F. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. It describes heat loss from exposed skin; it does not make an object colder than the air temperature. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

WC = 35.74 + 0.6215T − 35.75V^0.16 + 0.4275T V^0.16
A worked example

At 30°F with 10 mph wind, the standard equation gives a wind chill near 21°F.

Frequently asked questions

Does wind chill cool objects below air temperature?

It describes heat loss from exposed skin; it does not make an object colder than the air temperature.

When is the formula valid?

The NWS formulation is intended for air temperatures at or below 50°F and wind speeds above 3 mph.
